source.title: Scaling Laws for Conditional Emergence of Multilingual Image Captioning via Generalization from Translation
source.authors: Julian Spravil; Sebastian Houben; Sven Behnke

record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law measurements to multilingual vision-language models and conditional image-captioning generalization, rather than reproducing language-model pretraining scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study measures test cross-entropy across model sizes, training samples, and compute, and relates that loss to downstream performance. It extrapolates to a hypothetical 30B model, but does not evaluate a larger run to validate that prediction. It does not test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or architectural shape effects.
record.test_reason: The study fits power laws to held-out losses from multilingual VLM continuous pretraining and relates those losses to downstream performance, testing V5 and V6. Its finding that omitting initial multilingual loss biases the fit, and its comparison with published cross-lingual scaling results, also bear on V7. It does not directly test text-only language-model pretraining under V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that multilingual VLM transfer loss depends on initial multilinguality, model size and seen samples, with different predictor importance across tasks. Zero-shot unseen-language captioning still requires a language prefix despite lower CE loss; fine-tuning with full task-language coverage removes that requirement and produces competitive downstream results. They restrict their scaling laws to this experimental setup and acknowledge only 16 configurations.
record.recipe_differences: Uses multilingual encoder-decoder VLMs, CE loss on task-language splits, Pareto-frontier compute fits and multivariate OLS fits, rather than the original language-model scaling setup. The paper says its laws are specific to its experimental setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling relationships differ by test split/task: sample count dominates the ST fit, while model size and samples have negative associations for SC and UC. UC loss is nearly flat or slightly non-monotonic at higher sample counts for some model sizes.
record.problems: The scaling-law analysis uses only 16 experimental configurations. The authors say the derived laws are specific to their setup and note possible effects from language count, pretraining, synthetic data/style-domain gaps, task difficulty, and multiple tasks. The 30B estimate is extrapolated, not validated on a run. Downstream fits use a limited number of measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. The downstream results are summarized using the explicit aggregate conclusions and the stated R2 = 0.52 result rather than extracting every Figure 5 panel.

untested.parts: Text-only language-model held-out pretraining loss with non-bottlenecked scaling axes over several orders of magnitude.
No prediction fitted on small runs is validated on runs orders of magnitude larger. The hypothetical 30B model is not trained; leave-one-out validation is not this extrapolation test.
No fitted compute-optimal parameter/sample allocation as a function of budget. Selecting a loss-compute Pareto frontier does not establish allocation exponents.
No architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Modalities and regimes outside the tested multilingual encoder-decoder VLM continuous-pretraining setting; no general demonstration for video or repeated-data training.
Prospective downstream prediction on substantially larger models and downstream tasks outside the reported benchmarks.
Compute-optimal split sensitivity, parameter-counting and schedule ablations, and systematic comparisons of alternative curve families are not tested.

missing.what: Baseline P,S-only fit is reported as biased when initial multilingual loss T is omitted; retain this explicit fit-specification result without inventing unavailable baseline coefficients.
SC parameter-versus-sample coefficient difference is 0.13 with 95% CI [-0.09,0.35]; authors explicitly contrast this with published model-size dominance in cross-lingual LLM continuous pretraining.
Multivariate fit R2 and leave-one-out R2: SC 0.982/0.965, ST 0.935/0.873, UC 0.965/0.936. These distinguish fitted associations from the unvalidated 30B extrapolation.
Pretraining-scale disambiguation accuracy is explicitly reported as constant; mean accuracy is approximately 53.6, 54.1, 54.3 and 53.5% across the four model sizes.

Without a language prefix, unseen-language XM3600 CIDEr remains about 0.8–0.9 across scale; with the prefix it rises from 1.7 to 26.6. Loss improvements therefore predict usable generation only conditionally on inference prompting.

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. V1 links were removed because the measured systems and regime fall under V5. Raw loss reductions contribute to scaling series but do not independently establish power-law form. The compute fits use selected Pareto-frontier points. Figure 2's extracted equation placement is ambiguous, but coefficient magnitudes and Section 4.1 resolve UC/ST assignment. Figure 5 panel details are declared aggregated in rows_left_out, so they are identified for splitting in row fixes and verdict reasons rather than listed as wholly omitted results.

versions.untested_parts: The tested systems are multilingual encoder-decoder VLMs in a specific synthetic-data setup, not general language models. It does not establish scaling over several orders of magnitude or test each parameter, token, and compute axis independently with the other two held non-bottlenecked.
No larger run is evaluated against a prediction fitted on smaller runs; the 30B result is an extrapolation only.
No fixed-compute search for a loss-minimising parameter/token allocation is reported.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.

The study covers multilingual image-captioning VLMs and its continuous-pretraining/fine-tuning setting only; it does not test other modalities such as video, repeated data, or general transfer regimes.
Downstream relationships are evaluated for the reported translation, captioning, and disambiguation tasks only; some task/model fits are weak.

The paper notes setup specificity and differing predictor patterns across task splits, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, data, schedule, or fitting choices, test disagreements between published laws, or show curves bending away from a single power law.

conditions.value: Multi30K translation, CoMMuTE translation and disambiguation, COCO Karpathy, Multi30K captioning, XM3600
downstream performance versus UC/ST/SC CE loss

rows.measure: fit of downstream-performance trends against CE loss
rows.value: Strong to moderate fit for most tasks; lower CE loss generally corresponded to better downstream performance.
rows.note: The authors caution that the number of measurements is limited.
rows.check: The stated strong-to-moderate association supports V6 for most tasks. Split out the weak and absent relationships rather than treating the aggregate as uniformly partial.

rows.subject: Evaluated models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Regressed downstream task performance on CE loss for the reported task conditions.

conditions.value: English and German tasks with full task-language coverage; unseen-language Multi30K captioning

rows.measure: fit of downstream-performance trends against CE loss
rows.value: Weaker fits for English and German tasks with full coverage; R2 = 0.52 for unseen-language Multi30K captioning.
rows.note: The paper attributes weaker full-coverage fits partly to performance nearing or reaching a plateau.
rows.check: The R2=0.52 panel is XM3600 unseen-language captioning, not Multi30K. Section 5.1 itself misnames the dataset; Figure 5 and the evaluation datasets resolve this. Separate near-zero fits from moderate fits.

relationships.condition: Pareto-frontier compute scaling for multilingual VLM continuous pretraining
relationships.reason: Corrected L49–L51 report decreasing power-law loss fits for UC, ST and SC, with R2=0.87, 0.95 and 0.98 respectively.
relationships.display_finding: Decreasing compute power laws fitted UC, ST and SC losses with R² of 0.87, 0.95 and 0.98, respectively.

relationships.condition: Conditional parameter/sample scaling for seen captioning and unseen-language captioning
relationships.reason: L52–L53 and L57–L58 show significant negative model-size and sample coefficients in the multivariate power-law fits.
relationships.display_finding: Multivariate power-law fits had significantly negative model-size and sample coefficients for both seen and unseen-language captioning.

relationships.condition: Unseen-language captioning as samples increase at fixed model size
relationships.reason: L11–L12, L24, L34–L36 and L46–L48 show flattening or small increases at higher sample counts despite the aggregate compute-frontier fit.
relationships.display_finding: At higher sample sizes, unseen-language captioning curves flattened or increased slightly despite the aggregate compute-frontier fit.

relationships.condition: Seen translation, model-size effect conditional on samples and initial loss
relationships.reason: L55 has no significant model-size effect, whereas L56 shows a clear sample effect; the authors suggest an encoder bottleneck.
relationships.display_finding: Model size had no significant effect, whereas additional samples clearly helped, suggesting an encoder bottleneck.

relationships.reason: L59 and Figure 5 show improving performance with lower pretraining CE, including translation fits with R2=0.73–0.97.
relationships.display_finding: Most downstream performance improved with lower pretraining cross-entropy, including translation fits with R² of 0.73–0.97.

relationships.condition: Several full-coverage captioning tasks and XM3600 unseen-language captioning
relationships.reason: Corrected L60 and Figure 5 show weak full-coverage fits, including R2=0.22 and 0.26, and a moderate unseen-language XM3600 fit of 0.52.
relationships.display_finding: Full-coverage captioning fits included R² values of 0.22 and 0.26, while unseen-language XM3600 achieved 0.52.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned CoMMuTE German disambiguation predicted from ST loss
relationships.reason: Figure 5 reports R2=0.03, providing essentially no loss-based predictive relationship; this panel needs a separate row.
relationships.display_finding: Pretraining ST loss explained essentially none of the fine-tuned German disambiguation variation, with R²=0.03.

relationships.reason: Section 5.1 explicitly reports constant accuracy with pretraining scale; Table 13 gives mean accuracies near 54% across sizes. No row captures this condition.
relationships.display_finding: Before downstream fine-tuning, mean accuracy remained near 54% across pretraining sizes.

relationships.condition: Task setting and base-model multilingual pretraining in the multivariate loss fit
relationships.reason: L52–L58 show task-dependent predictor effects; Section 4 additionally states that omitting initial multilingual loss biases the fit, a result missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Predictor effects varied by task, and omitting initial multilingual loss biased the multivariate fit.

relationships.condition: Multimodal seen-captioning scaling compared with published cross-lingual LLM scaling
relationships.reason: Section 4.1 finds no distinguishable parameter-versus-sample dominance (difference 0.13, CI [-0.09,0.35]), explicitly differing from Zheng et al.; this comparison is missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Seen-captioning showed no distinguishable parameter-versus-sample dominance, with a difference of 0.13 and confidence interval [−0.09, 0.35], differing from published cross-lingual results.

reader_labels.label: supports
